reference: DOS6 inc/path.asm (Path_Crunch, Search, Search_Ftype and environment search), full module comparison.
changes: Normalize declarations, procedures and instruction indentation to tabs; replace reconstruction-provenance sentence with module description and add original-style entry/exit comments matching current interfaces. No copyright/authorship invented.
necessity: A cohesive counterpart of the original standalone PATH helper module, not a single-symbol fragment. Keep it separate from neighbouring logpart/mblate. Four related routines share path buffer and extension strings. No second PATH-search implementation found in BIOS source by named-symbol search; no external named callers found either, which does not justify deleting target-resident bytes.
differences: DOS7 uses byte-aligned SysInitSeg, local path/find buffer, explicit segment setup and config_envlen/config_wrkseg instead of PSP environment lookup. Search flag handling and register preservation differ from DOS6 and remain unchanged; preserve exact target behavior rather than substituting reference instructions.

validation.reason: All 166 effective assembler statements unchanged, including quoted string contents and explicit cmp encoding.
validation.binary_baseline: P11 BIOS/IO.SYS and T11 COMMAND.COM/MSDOS.SYS exact acceptance retained.
